plan.title: Notewise launch
plan.summary: A fictional 3-person team launches Notewise, an AI note-taking app for independent consultants, via founder-led LinkedIn content and live demos. Goal: 500 paying users in 12 months.
plan.decision: Commit a 6-month runway and a Q3 public launch on a LinkedIn-only acquisition bet.

assumptions.statement: LinkedIn founder content will drive 60% of signups at a 3% visitor-to-trial rate.
Consultants will pay $20/mo once they try the product for a week.
The team can ship a reliable v1 by the Q3 date with current headcount.
Incumbent note apps will not ship a comparable AI feature within the year.

failure_modes.title: LinkedIn channel under-delivers
failure_modes.story: By month 5 the founder's posting cadence collapsed under launch crunch; reach fell 70% and the single-channel funnel produced a fraction of the planned trials.
failure_modes.indicator: Weekly trial signups from LinkedIn vs. plan
failure_modes.threshold: Below 50% of the weekly trial target for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_modes.response: Open a second channel (consultant communities / referral) and book a content backup author
failure_modes.mitigation: Pre-build a 6-week content buffer and line up a second acquisition channel before launch, not after

failure_modes.title: Trials do not convert to paid
failure_modes.story: Users liked the demo but week-1 activation was weak; without a clear in-product 'aha', trial-to-paid stalled at 4% and unit economics never closed.
failure_modes.indicator: Trial-to-paid conversion and week-1 activation rate
failure_modes.threshold: Trial-to-paid below 8%, or week-1 activation below 30%, for two cohorts
failure_modes.response: Pause paid acquisition, run 5 activation interviews, ship one onboarding fix per week
failure_modes.mitigation: Define and instrument the activation event before launch; gate scale-up on hitting it

failure_modes.title: v1 slips past Q3
failure_modes.story: Sync and reliability bugs pushed the launch two months; the content runway burned with no product to convert it, wasting the only acquisition window.
failure_modes.indicator: Burndown against the Q3 scope and open P0 bug count
failure_modes.threshold: Scope burndown behind by >2 weeks at the T-6-week checkpoint
failure_modes.response: Cut scope to the activation-critical path; delay non-essential features post-launch
failure_modes.mitigation: Freeze a minimal launch scope tied to the activation event; everything else is post-launch

failure_modes.title: Incumbent ships comparable AI
failure_modes.story: A large note app shipped a similar AI feature in month 8, compressing the differentiation window before Notewise had a retention moat.
failure_modes.indicator: Incumbent release notes and feature announcements
failure_modes.threshold: Any incumbent ships a comparable AI note feature
failure_modes.response: Lean into the consultant-specific workflow moat; accelerate the integrations roadmap
failure_modes.mitigation: Build a narrow consultant-workflow wedge that a horizontal incumbent is unlikely to copy quickly

residual_risk: Even with mitigations, the plan still rests on a single founder's content output as the primary growth engine for the first two quarters. If the founder is unavailable for an extended period, no mitigation fully covers the gap; the team accepts this knowingly and revisits at the 6-month mark.
